articles.title: Burnham to visit Ukraine with promise of boost for Kyiv’s long-range missiles
articles.excerpt:
PM will use independence day trip to announce sharing of classified information about Storm Shadow components

Britain will boost Ukraine’s capacity to make its own long-range missiles, Andy Burnham w...
articles.body_text:
PM will use independence day trip to announce sharing of classified information about Storm Shadow components

Britain will boost Ukraine’s capacity to make its own long-range missiles, Andy Burnham will announce on Monday, as he travels to Kyiv for the country’s independence day on his first foreign visit as prime minister.

Burnham will arrive in the Ukrainian capital on Monday morning at a crucial time in the war, with Kyiv braced for another wave of Russian missile attacks and the country’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, facing his most direct domestic challenge.

The UK prime minister will use the trip to announce that the UK government will allow the European defence company MBDA to declassify information about UK-made components of the Anglo-French Storm Shadow/Scalp missiles to help Ukraine build its own version.

While the announcement will probably take years to have an impact on the war, it is likely to escalate tensions with Moscow at an already fraught moment in UK-Russian relations.

Burnham said in a statement on Sunday night: “On Ukraine’s 35th anniversary of independence, the Ukrainian people should be in no doubt: the UK is behind you today and for as long as it takes.

“I am proud of the contribution our country has made to Ukraine and I want the Ukrainian people to hear it directly from me that our support will not waver. After all, Ukraine’s security is our security.

“The friendship between our two countries will long outlast Russia’s illegal war. In both the fight and in the rebuilding to come, we will stand with Ukraine and deliver opportunities for people across both our countries.

“Russia should be in no doubt of our resolve. We will not back down until there is a just and lasting peace.”

Burnham will announce in Kyiv that the UK will help France set up assembly lines in Ukraine for long-range missiles, which the French president, Emmanuel Macron, promised last month.

Macron spoke to Zelenskyy on Saturday to promise to deliver separate interceptor missiles, which could help counter the recent barrage of high-speed Russian missile attacks on Kyiv.

Meanwhile, European leaders have condemned Friday’s drone attack on a busy shopping centre in central Ukraine, which killed 16 people in Zelenskyy’s home town of Kryvyi Rih.

The Ukrainian military has run out of US-made Patriot interceptors, and the US president, Donald Trump, recently backtracked on a promise to let Ukraine build its own.

However, Zelenskyy said over the weekend he still wanted to buy more US-made Patriots, adding that Ukraine was happy to pay for them rather than receive them as military aid. “I wanted to secure 300 Patriot missiles for the winter package,” he said. “The request from our air force is 360.”

He added that he had reached an agreement with France on at least one air-defence system ​this year, and with ‌Germany on the supply of ​about 600 ​interceptors in 2027-28.

Macron posted on X on Saturday: “It is crucial to provide Ukraine with all the necessary means to defend its skies and thwart this aggression … It is essential that all countries with capabilities at their disposal also join this effort.”

The British announcement is a small step in a much larger and longer-term project that could lead to Ukraine making its own long-range versions of the Storm Shadow cruise missile in several years’ time.

But the move is likely to trigger further criticism from Moscow at a time when tensions between the UK and Russia are already high.

Last week, Russia accused the UK of deliberately escalating the conflict by allowing Ukraine to launch attacks with British-made drones, warning that the deeper Britain’s involvement, “the higher the price it will pay”.

This weekend it emerged that Russia had withdrawn its ambassador in London without naming a replacement, prompting speculation it was downgrading its diplomatic presence in the UK.

Burnham has insisted that Russian threats will not weaken British support for Ukraine, saying last week: “We are not fair-weather friends. We will be there in Ukraine’s hour of need, and that won’t change.”

The prime minister will on Monday use a meeting of the coalition of the willing, which comprises 34 countries that have promised to help secure Ukraine in the event of a peace deal with Russia, to underline that commitment.

The meeting will be co-chaired by Burnham and Macron, who will join remotely via video link. Friedrich Merz, the German chancellor, will also take part in the call as the leaders discuss ways to help Ukraine repel the recent wave of long-distance attacks.

While there, Burnham will attend independence day events, the details of which are being kept secret amid concerns of a major Russian attack, and receive an award in recognition of the UK’s support for Ukraine.

Zelenskyy is facing the most concerted internal political challenge of his presidency after the call for an election by his former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov.

The Ukrainian president responded to Fedorov’s dramatic announcement for the first time this weekend, telling reporters on Saturday that holding elections, which have been suspended since the war began, risked splitting the country.

“I believe that if we want to destroy the country, then during such a war we can move in the selection of elections,” he said in a briefing to selected journalists that was held on Saturday, but details of which were reported on Sunday.

“I believe that during such a war, elections in general are big risks. Elections right now are a tsunami for the state that will split Ukraine,” he added.

articles.title: UK productivity growing faster than official figures suggest, thinktank finds
articles.excerpt:
Resolution Foundation suggests economy may finally be emerging from shadow of 2008 financial crisis

Productivity in the UK – a vital measure of economic health – is growing more strongly than officia...
articles.body_text:
Resolution Foundation suggests economy may finally be emerging from shadow of 2008 financial crisis

Productivity in the UK – a vital measure of economic health – is growing more strongly than official figures suggest, according to analysis from the Resolution Foundation.

The thinktank suggests the chancellor, John Healey, may have inherited an economy finally starting to emerge from the long shadow of the 2008 global financial crisis.

Productivity measures the economic output produced by each worker, and is a crucial determinant of growth.

The Resolution Foundation reconsiders the UK’s recent productivity record, using what it argues is a more accurate snapshot of the workforce than the widely criticised labour force survey.

Simon Pittaway, the thinktank’s principal economist, said: “Britain’s dismal productivity record since the global financial crisis explains a lot of its economic stagnation and weak living standards growth.

“But while official figures suggest that the output of workers has worsened further in the mid-2020s, our more accurate productivity measure suggests that it has been improving in recent years.”

Some economists have argued the potential uptick in productivity has resulted from job cuts in relatively low-skilled sectors such as hospitality and retail, meaning the average worker has become more productive.

However, the thinktank rejects that idea, pointing out that the share of the workforce employed in hospitality is no lower now than it was in the late 2010s, and only just below its post-pandemic peak.

It also suggests the uptick cannot just be AI-related, as it is more widespread across different sectors of the UK economy.

Pittaway said: “Some have suggested that recent productivity gains have been driven by an early AI boom, and workers leaving low-productivity sectors like retail and hospitality. But nether explanation is borne out by the data. Instead, the UK’s productivity recovery has been achieved by the same workers, doing the same jobs, and working in the same sectors.”

The Resolution Foundation’s report was the latest to paint a relatively optimistic picture of the economy, after official figures last week showed the UK was the joint fastest-growing economy in the G7 in the first half of 2026.

John Van Reenen, Rachel Reeves’s former chief economic adviser, recently published a blogpost pointing to a similar productivity rethink by him and his colleagues at the London School of Economics.

Economists at Morgan Stanley said in a recent research note that the UK was now in “an OK place”. In a note titled “The vibes they are a-changin’”, its chief UK economist, Bruna Skarica, pointed out that growth and inflation had been hit less hard than feared by the Iran war, and consumer confidence had reached a two-year high.

articles.title: Government vows to make business rate valuations for pubs and hotels fairer
articles.excerpt:
Review will look at improving system for English and Welsh hospitality venues before next revaluation date in 2029

The government has promised that business rate valuations will be “made fairer” for ...
articles.body_text:
Review will look at improving system for English and Welsh hospitality venues before next revaluation date in 2029

The government has promised that business rate valuations will be “made fairer” for pubs and hotels in England and Wales, as Andy Burnham faces growing calls to help the UK’s struggling hospitality sector.

An independent review for England and Wales will look at improving the system for hospitality venues, which were hit by higher business rate bills this year after the end of pandemic-era relief and when new revaluations took effect.

It comes after Burnham announced last month that he would cut business rates for pubs, social clubs and live music venues in England by 20% from April next year.

The government has faced calls to reduce the tax burden on hospitality businesses, which have also struggled to cope with rising energy and food bills in recent years.

The review, which will be led by Jerry Schurder, an independent business rates specialist, will report back to the Treasury by the end of March 2027. It will consider valuations before the next revaluation date in 2029. The rise in valuations this year will not be affected.

James Murray, the financial secretary to the Treasury, said: “Pubs and hotels are vital for communities and bringing growth to every postcode,” adding that a “rethink of valuations” would help “build a fairer system for the future”.

Allen Simpson, the chief executive of the trade body UKHospitality, said it was positive the government was looking seriously at the valuation methodology for pubs and hotels.

“Business rates remain a significant burden for hospitality businesses, and the system needs to better reflect the trading realities for the sector,” he said.

Emma McClarkin, the chief executive of the British Beer & Pub Association, said the review was “sorely needed and hugely welcome” as pubs had for years “paid a disproportionately higher business rates bill which has ground down their ability to keep the doors open”.

While cuts have been welcomed by business owners, the industry has repeatedly called for the reform of the whole business rates system. Estimates suggest that two pubs are closing a day across Britain this year, hit by higher taxes, wages, energy and food costs.

Burnham is also facing calls to extend the business rates relief aimed at pubs, clubs and live music venues to bookshops. This month 234 independent booksellers signed an open letter calling on the prime minister to give bookshops the same consideration as other businesses that play a positive role in their communities.

The government has suggested that it will reform business rates, including small business rates relief, at John Healey’s first budget on 28 October.

articles.title: Tom Homan fires back at Florida Democrat over 'ridiculous' ICE racial profiling claim
articles.excerpt: White House border czar Tom Homan slams Florida candidate Angie Nixon over accusations that ICE racially profiles Black Americans. Speaking with Kayleigh McEnany on Saturday in America, Homan defends ...
articles.body_text:
White House border czar Tom Homan slams Florida candidate Angie Nixon over accusations that ICE racially profiles Black Americans. Speaking with Kayleigh McEnany on Saturday in America, Homan defends law enforcement officers and warns that sanctuary city policies release dangerous illegal aliens back into the public. He highlights the agency's efforts to target these sanctuary areas directly.

Border czar Tom Homan rejected Florida Democratic Senate nominee Angie Nixon’s warning that Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents would racially profile Black Americans, calling the accusation "ridiculous" and insisting immigration agents do not target people based on skin color.

"We don't arrest people based on the color of their skin. I'm actually an equal opportunity deporter. I deported people to 180 countries last year," Homan said on "Saturday in America."

"I don't care if you're from Asia, you're from Europe or you’re from other countries. If you're in the country illegally, you will be deported, regardless of the color of your skin," he added.

WHO IS ANGIE NIXON? BULLHORN-WIELDING SOCIALIST UPSETS ESTABLISHMENT FAVORITE IN SUNSHINE STATE STUNNER

Tom Homan, White House border czar, speaks to reporters outside the White House in Washington, D.C., on Friday, Nov. 14, 2025. (Eric Lee/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Nixon, who recently won Florida’s Democratic primary, lists ending detention centers and abolishing ICE among her key policy priorities, arguing that mass incarceration and mass deportation are "moral failures."

She also argues ICE "cannot be trusted with the power it has" and that the agency’s "terror tactics" should be dismantled, according to her campaign website.

"It's just lie, after lie, after lie, to try to vilify the men and women of ICE," Homan said.

Nixon made additional remarks on a recent episode of the "QNA: Questions Need Answers" podcast, where she said Republicans are "literally trying to kill us" and further criticized ICE.

HOMAN BLASTS DEM HYPOCRISY ON DEPORTATIONS, RECALLS PAST WHEN 'OBAMA GAVE ME AN AWARD' FOR ENFORCING BORDER

HALLANDALE, FLORIDA - AUGUST 17: Democratic U.S. Senate candidate, Florida state Rep. Angie Nixon speaks during a visit to the Ebenezer Missionary Baptist Church on August 17, 2026 in Hallandale Beach, Florida. Nixon, who previously protested on the floor of the state House with a bullhorn after Republicans redrew district lines, vies with retired Lt. Col. Alex Vindman in the August 18 primary. The winner is likely to face incumbent Republican U.S. Sen. Ashley Moody (R-FL) in the November general election. (Joe Raedle/Getty Images)

"Like, actually state-sanctioned violence. They’ve been doing it in the Black community. And they’re doing it even more so now with ICE. ICE is now a weaponized paramilitary force that is designed to terrorize us," she said.

Homan doubled down in defense of the federal immigration agency, maintaining that agents follow the law when conducting enforcement operations.

"That's a ridiculous statement," Homan said. "We don't racially profile. Everybody we talk to, we have reasonable suspicion of aliens to talk to them and to arrest them we need probable cause. That's what the law says. And that's what we do."

ICE MAKES NATIONWIDE ARRESTS OF ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS, MURDERERS, PEDOPHILES IN HOLIDAY BLITZ

An exterior view of a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) administrative office and processing center on June 28, 2025. (Paul Weaver/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)

The border czar blamed sanctuary policies for incidents of violence that have occurred during enforcement operations, like Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, who was fatally shot in July as agents tried to arrest him in Houston.

Homan argued that the policies increase risks associated with immigration enforcement, saying they prevent agents from taking custody of illegal immigrants while they are incarcerated, forcing officers to instead conduct arrests in communities.

"What sanctuary cities do is not only... give sanctuaries to criminals, it makes the community less safe because they're releasing public safety threats back into the public," he said.

"It puts our officers at greater risk. It puts the alien at greater risk because anything can happen during a street arrest," Homan added.

The Department of Homeland Security similarly rejected Nixon’s racial profiling allegations, telling Fox News Digital on Friday that her comments are "disgusting, reckless and categorically FALSE."

DHS also said immigration status determines who is targeted for enforcement, not race or ethnicity.

Nora Moriarty is a Writer at Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Nationals outfielder does his best Spider-Man impression for one of baseball's best catches of the year
articles.excerpt:
Baseball legend Johnny Damon shares prospects for an Orlando MLB team and talks about who he roots for on 'Fox News Saturday Night.'

Washington Nationals outfielder Jacob Young pulled off a remarkabl...
articles.body_text:
Baseball legend Johnny Damon shares prospects for an Orlando MLB team and talks about who he roots for on 'Fox News Saturday Night.'

Washington Nationals outfielder Jacob Young pulled off a remarkable Spider-Man impression with one of the most incredible catches of the baseball season on Sunday.

During the third inning of the Nationals’ 6-2 loss to the Miami Marlins at loanDepot Park, Young turned into Peter Parker.

The Marlins were up 1-0 in the bottom of the third inning with one out and a runner on first base. Marlins outfielder Heriberto Hernández ripped Nationals starting pitcher Jackson Kent’s 86-mph slider deep to left-center field.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Washington Nationals center fielder Jacob Young catches a fly ball hit by Miami Marlins left fielder Heriberto Hernandez and throws to second for a double play during the third inning Sunday, Aug. 23, 2026, in Miami. (AP Photo/Lynne Sladky)

Young got an outstanding read on the deep fly ball and slowed down just before the tall left-center field wall to time his jump with the ball. He then jumped into the wall, planted his right leg on the mesh fence to vault himself higher, used his right hand to further propel himself upward and snared the ball at the top of the wall.

Marlins shortstop Otto Lopez was the runner on first base, and he was off to the races when the ball was hit, thinking there was no chance Young could possibly catch Hernández’s deep fly ball. Lopez stood on third base, dumbfounded, as Young fired the ball back to first base to complete the spectacular inning-ending double play.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Jacob Young No. 30 of the Washington Nationals high-fives teammates in the dugout after scoring in the ninth inning against the Miami Marlins at loanDepot park on Aug. 21, 2026, in Miami, Fla. (JC Ruiz/Getty Images)

Young has been one of the best defensive center fielders in the sport since he entered the league toward the end of the 2023 season. This season has been the most productive for him offensively, as he has a .244 batting average with 10 home runs and 43 RBI.

While the numbers aren’t eye-popping, he had a combined five home runs over the first three years of his career, making this year’s offensive output a marked improvement.

Jacob Young of the Washington Nationals catches a fly ball in the third inning against the Miami Marlins at loanDepot park on Aug. 21, 2026, in Miami, Fla. (JC Ruiz/Getty Images)

The 27-year-old is incredibly fast, making him a very valuable player for the Nationals.

While the Nationals may have lost the game, Young’s catch will be remembered for a long time.

Ryan Canfield is a digital production assistant for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Australia news live: KMPG axes hundreds of staff in wake of audit leaks scandal; jobseeker now barely two-thirds of pension
articles.excerpt:
Audit and consulting giant reports revenue fall of 1% year-on-year. Follow today’s news live

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

KPMG Australia is cutting 27 partners and abo...
articles.body_text:
Audit and consulting giant reports revenue fall of 1% year-on-year. Follow today’s news live

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

KPMG Australia is cutting 27 partners and about 360 employees in the wake of an audit leaks scandal that saw it cut off from new government contracts.

The audit and consulting giant today reported its revenue fell 1% year-on-year, to $2.26bn in the year 2025-26.

While the embattled audit arm had seen revenue grow 11%, its consulting revenue was down 16.9%. Most of the workers to be let go are from the consulting arm.

KPMG’s new chief executive, John Sams, said weak demand for its services was expected to continue beyond the next 12 months, blaming Australia’s weak economy. He said:

double quotation markThe professional services sector is also changing rapidly as client expectations evolve, AI reshapes the way services are delivered and government spending on consultants remains lower. We also recognise the challenges created by our own failings, and the work we must continue to do to rebuild trust …

After careful consideration, we have made the difficult decision to reduce our workforce and restructure parts of the firm. This is not a decision that has been taken lightly, and we know it will have a very real impact on people.

The firm said it was discussing further cuts to a small number of award-based jobs. Sams said KPMG would continue to assess its operating environment as it sought to stay financially sustainable. You can read about the firm’s difficulties here:

Victorian Bar lashes Liberal plan to split the court of appeal

The Victorian Bar, which represents the thousands of barristers practising in the state, has lashed the Liberal party’s election commitment to split the court of appeal in two.

The opposition leader, Jess Wilson, yesterday announced the plan to create a dedicated court of criminal appeal alongside a separate court of civil appeal, and to appoint additional judges to the latter to set precedents for tougher sentences.

Legal and civil rights groups yesterday criticised the plan as an attempt to politicise the courts, which are independent of government.

In a statement this afternoon, the Victorian Bar president, Fiona Ryan SC, said the state was “fortunate to have a judiciary that is independent and apolitical, and which applies the laws enacted by parliament without fear or favour, and without any regard to their personal views. That independence is essential to the rule of law”.

double quotation markThe Victorian Bar is deeply concerned about any threat to the independence of the judiciary. Courts must not be politicised. Judges must always be appointed on merit, and never with a view to influencing outcomes. Any suggestion that judges might be appointed to influence outcomes is to be condemned in the strongest terms. It is anathema to the separation of powers, which is the foundation of community confidence in the independence of the courts.

Ryan said while the group welcomes increased resources for the courts and judges, “is not yet clear how splitting the Court of Appeal will improve the administration of justice”.

Diesel prices back above $2.50 a litre in some cities

Diesel prices are back near recent highs of above $2.50 a litre as oil markets wait for the US to announce possible Iran sanctions.

Diesel in Melbourne is 255.4 cents per litre today, back where it was at the start of August, according to MotorMouth. Sydney has climbed to 247.1 cents, Brisbane is at 252.2 and Hobart 254.7.

Service stations have hiked their prices as wholesale and import prices rise. Commonwealth Bank analyst Vivek Dhar wrote today that Singapore diesel benchmark prices have kept spiking higher.

Oil production in the Gulf has recovered somewhat since the US went to war with Iran but diesel refining in the area has not, Dhar wrote.

Global diesel prices have also been particularly under pressure as Ukrainian strikes have disrupted exports from Russia, which had been a stopgap. Dhar predicted diesel prices would be slower to return to normal than oil in the coming year.

Oil prices are still volatile. The Brent crude oil benchmark has spent nearly a week above US$90 a barrel. The US is expected to announce new economic sanctions on Iran and allies on Monday US time.

Dhar said CBA expects Brent oil futures to trade between US$70‑100 a barrel in the next four months. While US$70 might seem low, he says the oil market was already oversupplied before the war and will be again even if just 50% of trade through the strait of Hormuz resumes.

The NSW premier, Chris Minns, says he supports extending the royal commission on antisemitism after calls for an extension by the federal opposition were rejected by the Albanese government.

The royal commission, established following the Bondi attack, is holding its final scheduled hearing block this week. Last week, the shadow federal education minister and prominent Jewish MP Julian Leeser brought an unsuccessful motion to extend its reporting date to allow it to hear from further witnesses. This morning, the shadow home affairs minister Jonno Duniam reiterated the call to extend the royal commission on ABC Radio National.

At a press conference today, Minns said he had spoken to senior members of the Jewish community who were “satisfied both with the hearing they got and the platform that enabled them to make their case”, but did support an extension to allow further witnesses to appear. He said:

double quotation markGiven the expense and time that’s gone into the royal commission, and the fact that we’re not going to have another one, at least for a long period of time, and we are using this royal commission to get to the fundamental truths of what happened on the day, and also what happened in the lead-up to that day, particularly around antisemitism, I’m hopeful that it will speak to as large a number of people as possible, and genuinely get the perspective of the community.

If we need to go a couple of weeks longer, given that most of the expense was spent setting it up, that would seem to be money well spent because both the federal and the state government are relying on these recommendations to shape some of our policy.

Prior to Anthony Albanese’s announcement of the federal royal commission, Minns had announced plans for a state-led commission, which was superseded by the national inquiry.

KPMG Australia is cutting 27 partners and about 360 employees in the wake of an audit leaks scandal that saw it cut off from new government contracts.

The audit and consulting giant today reported its revenue fell 1% year-on-year, to $2.26bn in the year 2025-26.

While the embattled audit arm had seen revenue grow 11%, its consulting revenue was down 16.9%. Most of the workers to be let go are from the consulting arm.

KPMG’s new chief executive, John Sams, said weak demand for its services was expected to continue beyond the next 12 months, blaming Australia’s weak economy. He said:

double quotation markThe professional services sector is also changing rapidly as client expectations evolve, AI reshapes the way services are delivered and government spending on consultants remains lower. We also recognise the challenges created by our own failings, and the work we must continue to do to rebuild trust …

After careful consideration, we have made the difficult decision to reduce our workforce and restructure parts of the firm. This is not a decision that has been taken lightly, and we know it will have a very real impact on people.

The firm said it was discussing further cuts to a small number of award-based jobs. Sams said KPMG would continue to assess its operating environment as it sought to stay financially sustainable. You can read about the firm’s difficulties here:

Leah Stewart recounts shark bite: ‘I’ll never forget its face’

Leah Stewart, the woman bitten by a shark at Sydney’s Coogee beach in June, will appear on next Sunday’s episode of 60 Minutes. A short clip of the interview includes the mother recounting coming face-to-face with a great white shark.

double quotation markIts face was horrific. I’ll never forget its face. It was a monster.

It was holding on to my leg, and I just thought of August. And I thought, ‘she’s not going to have a mum, she’s going to grow up without a mum’.

I couldn’t handle that, I didn’t want her not to have a mum.

Stewart went on to say: “I just thought I’ve got to, I’ve got to fight it. Do everything I can to be here.”

Australia’s unemployment payments have fallen so far behind the pension they now amounts to just 68% of the payment, a new research paper released today by the Australian Council for Social Services (ACOSS) has revealed.

A person aged 67 who is eligible for the age pension receives $600 a week, but a 66-year-old who loses their job receives just $409 a week to cover the same basic living costs.

In the 1970s, jobseeker and the pension were paid at the same rate and by the early 90s, jobseeker was still about 90% of the pension. But in 1997, the Howard government legislated pensions to be benchmarked to 25% of male total average weekly earnings – but left unemployment payments out of that legislation.

Pensions have risen in line with wage growth many times while jobseeker has not, and the pension was increased in real terms by more than $30 a week in 2009.

Now the pension is 60% of the minimum wage, while jobseeker is just 40.6%.

ACOSS’s CEO, Cassandra Goldie, called on the federal government to raise the jobseeker rate to two-thirds of the minimum wage:

double quotation markA 66-year-old and a 67-year-old face exactly the same rent, grocery bill and energy costs. There is no reason one of them should be living on $191 a week less than the other.

Woefully low income support is causing physical and mental harm and trapping people in a cycle of poverty and deprivation.

People who receive jobseeker are skipping meals and forgoing essential medications just to keep a roof over their heads.

We are one of the wealthiest countries in the world yet successive governments choose to keep 3.7 million people living in poverty. We know how to fix this problem, we just need politicians to act.

Victoria police have identified a man found with critical injuries on a busy walking trail in Glenroy, about 14km from Melbourne’s CBD, on Sunday afternoon, as reported earlier in the blog.

double quotation markPolice would like to thank the media and public for their assistance. At this stage it is not believed he was assaulted, however the circumstances surrounding what has occurred is unclear.

The man remains in hospital in a serious condition.

We have some important photos of little penguins getting vaccinated against H5 bird flu to break up the day’s news:

Ampol’s profit soars on war-linked price surges

Oil refiner and petrol seller Ampol has seen its interim earnings jump after it managed to secure fuel supplies to capitalise on the impact of the Middle East conflict on energy prices, AAP reports.

Net profit on a replacement cost basis – which excludes the impact of oil prices on inventories – jumped more than four times to $857.2m in the six months ended June 30, from $180.2m a year earlier.

Its statutory first-half result was even bigger at $1.4bn, against a loss of $25.3m in the first half of 2025.

Matt Halliday, the company’s chief executive, said:

double quotation markWhile the market dislocation provided a benefit to our financial results, our supply responsiveness, trading capabilities, refinery reliability, customer and supplier relationships, as well as the progress of our retail segmentation strategy all enabled Ampol to meet its customer needs.

Ampol is Australia’s largest transport fuel provider, accounting for about 15-20% of total refined fuel needs.

Apartment rents now cost more than half a typical worker’s take-home pay in all Australian capital cities

Renting a mid-priced unit in any of Australia’s capital cities now costs more than half a typical single worker’s take-home pay, spurring advocates to urge Labor to offer renters more protections.

New modelling shows someone earning $70,000 – close to the median annual income – would have to spend two-thirds of their earnings if they wanted to rent the median Sydney apartment.

Everybody’s Home, a housing advocacy group, released the analysis in its latest “Priced Out” report amid a political debate over rent hikes and the Albanese government’s tax reforms.

articles.title: Can Kenya’s AI ambitions coexist with Naivasha’s water needs?
articles.excerpt:
Naivasha, Kenya – For communities living around Naivasha, water is not an abstract resource. It sustains families, livestock, farms and schools.

That reality has taken on new significance after plans...
articles.body_text:
Naivasha, Kenya – For communities living around Naivasha, water is not an abstract resource. It sustains families, livestock, farms and schools.

That reality has taken on new significance after plans for a major Microsoft-G42 data centre in Olkaria, near Lake Naivasha, stalled in May 2026 over concerns about available power capacity.

Microsoft and United Arab Emirates-based artificial intelligence company G42 announced the project in 2024 as part of a $1bn digital investment package for Kenya. The proposed facility was to run on geothermal energy and eventually scale to as much as 1 gigawatt of capacity.

The uncertainty has also prompted questions about what another major industrial user could mean for water in a region where residents already report shortages.

Microsoft and G42 said the proposed data centre campus would run entirely on renewable geothermal energy and incorporate water conservation technology. The companies did not disclose a project-specific water consumption figure in their 2024 announcement.

Kenya Electricity Generating Company (KenGen) communications director Frank David Ochieng told Al Jazeera that the data centre remains at the design stage and that he could not comment further until the project is ready to proceed.

For residents like Musa Olorkedienye, who spoke to Al Jazeera, water scarcity is already a daily concern. He says communities around Olkaria have seen changes in access to water, including the loss of reliable piped supplies that residents previously received from KenGen.

“Currently, we are relying on water vendors to get water, our animals are walking for kilometres, and we fear things could get worse as demand for water rises,” Olorkedienye says.

Pastoralist Isaac Leshishi, who also spoke to Al Jazeera, says increasingly harsh weather is adding to the pressure.

The choice of Olkaria was closely tied to energy. The area is home to Kenya’s major geothermal operations, making it an attractive location for a power-intensive facility.

KenGen operates the Olkaria geothermal complex, while Microsoft and G42 planned to power the proposed data centre entirely with geothermal energy.

Naivasha is a freshwater lake in Kenya’s Rift Valley whose catchment supports agriculture, tourism, livestock and domestic water use. Its basin also hosts geothermal development and other economic activity.

Grace Kimani, a patrol leader with Lake Naivasha and Oloiden, told Al Jazeera that the reservoir is under growing pressure from population growth, agriculture, water abstraction, climate variability, pollution and ecosystem degradation.

“The planned Microsoft-G42 data centre in Olkaria could bring jobs and investment, but its water demand raises concerns about adding pressure to already competing needs, particularly during dry periods,” she said.

Kimani said there is limited public information about the project’s expected water demand, source and cooling technology. She said transparency and an assessment of its cumulative impact on water resources would be important.

She also called for water-efficient or water-free cooling, water recycling and the use of treated wastewater, as well as sustainable abstraction limits and community involvement in monitoring.

Silas Wanjala of the Lake Naivasha Riparian Association, who spoke to Al Jazeera, said the region is heavily dependent on groundwater and that declining water flows are adding to the pressure.

“These industries, especially EcoCloud, which deal with data, will consume a lot of water at a time when rivers are drying, and demand for water is on the rise,” Wanjala said.

Olkaria EcoCloud Data Centre is a local partner in the G42-led development. In 2024, the Kenya News Agency reported that G42, Microsoft and EcoCloud signed a letter of intent for the wider data-centre initiative, with EcoCloud described as a local partner that had previously signed a memorandum of understanding with G42.

Wanjala points to past fluctuations in Lake Naivasha as a warning.

“This lake in 2010 nearly dried up due to over-abstraction, and this could be repeated due to high demand for water by these investors in Olkaria,” he says.

His concern comes against a wider backdrop of water scarcity in Kenya. The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) of the United Nations says Kenya has about 527 cubic metres (527,000 litres) of freshwater available per person, below the 1,000-cubic-metre threshold for water scarcity, and estimates availability could fall to about 475 cubic metres per person by 2030.

The figures do not show what effect the proposed data centre would have on Lake Naivasha. They provide context, however, for why the prospect of another major water user is drawing scrutiny in a region where demand is already high.

The amount of water the proposed Microsoft-G42 facility itself would require remains unclear.

The project announcement provides no projected consumption figure.

Existing industrial use offers some context.

A KenGen environmental and social impact assessment records that 195,165 cubic metres of water were abstracted from Lake Naivasha in July 2023 for domestic and commercial uses at Olkaria and for operations and domestic use at Eburru.

Of that total, 153,918 cubic metres were used for commercial operations at Olkaria. The assessment records the abstraction as within Water Resources Authority (WRA) permitted levels.

Those figures relate to existing KenGen operations, not the proposed data centre.

For farmer Eskimos Kobia, who spoke to Al Jazeera, the potential competition extends beyond households and livestock. He says farmers, pastoralists, schools and investors will all face greater pressure as demand increases.

Kimani said climate variability has also led to fluctuations in lake levels, with periods of flooding followed by prolonged dry conditions.

“Water quality is affected by agricultural run-off, untreated wastewater in some areas and invasive species,” she says.

Not everyone in Naivasha opposes the investment.

Absolom Mukhuusi of the Naivasha Professional Association, who spoke to Al Jazeera, says the technology sector could bring jobs, infrastructure and new businesses to the area. But he says economic benefits should not come at the expense of local communities.

“Even as we welcome the investors, our biggest fear is what happens to our water bodies and communities as water is diverted to Olkaria for the heavy users,” he says.

Geologist Kenyatta Otieno, who spoke to Al Jazeera, sees another potential benefit.

He recalls the pressure large flower farms once placed on the lake’s ecosystem, saying many have since left or scaled back their operations.

Otieno says the proposed centre would have included a resource centre to monitor lake levels and weather patterns. Such monitoring, he says, could help identify the highest water level over time and guide riparian land zoning.

“The centre being built with water conservation in mind would be futuristic as Naivasha is generally a water-scarce area. It would be a model for future development,” Otieno said.

Kenya already has regulators responsible for managing competing demands. The WRA regulates water abstraction and issues water-use permits, while the National Environment Management Authority (NEMA) oversees environmental impact assessments under the country’s environmental regulatory framework.

Attempts by Al Jazeera to obtain comments from WRA and NEMA officials were unsuccessful. Efforts to reach Microsoft-G42 officials and Kenyan government officials for comment on the project’s status and water requirements were also unsuccessful.

For now, the project’s eventual scale, design and water requirements remain unclear, according to KenGen.

“We are now competing with the multibillion [-dollar] companies for water, and we fear that we shall be the losers in the long run,” Leshishi said.

articles.title: Ebola cases in DRC hit 5,515 as Pope Leo urges global action to save lives
articles.excerpt:
DR Congo miners risk Ebola to make a living

The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has reached  5,515 confirmed cases of infection and killed 2,642 people, with 51 new cases...
articles.body_text:
DR Congo miners risk Ebola to make a living

The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has reached  5,515 confirmed cases of infection and killed 2,642 people, with 51 new cases detected in Ituri and North Kivu provinces, according to the latest government figures.

The update on Sunday came as Pope Leo called for ⁠international action to help contain the epidemic, which is now the deadliest Ebola outbreak in the DRC’s history.

Declared in mid-May, it is the DRC’s 17th Ebola epidemic and was designated a Public Health Emergency of International Concern by the World Health Organization (WHO), its highest alert level, also covering neighbouring Uganda.

The outbreak is now on track to surpass the deadliest Ebola epidemic on record, which was the 2014–2016 outbreak in West Africa that killed more than 11,000 people.

According to government figures, the case fatality rate in the DRC has climbed from about 20 percent in early June to nearly 48 percent now, meaning almost one in two people infected are dying.

Contact tracing, however, has improved sharply, from 30 percent in June to more than 85 percent.

The disease has also proved deadly for those fighting it. About 160 health workers have been infected, and about 45 have died, according to the WHO.

Efforts to contain the outbreak, however, have been hampered by armed conflict in the affected provinces, displacement, attacks on medical personnel and facilities, a mobile working population and a lack of critical infrastructure.

There is no approved vaccine or treatment for this particular strain of Ebola, known as Bundibugyo, which is rarer than the virus type behind most past outbreaks.

The WHO has pledged 70,000 doses of the Ervebo vaccine, which is licensed for Ebola and has been effective in past outbreaks. According to the global body, early data from animal trials suggest it may offer some protection against Bundibugyo.

Some 16,250 doses of the vaccine arrived in the DRC on Friday.

WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus and other officials said the response in the DRC needs to be scaled up two to threefold to contain the outbreak and reach every affected area.

They also called for more support and protection for front-line health workers, including protective equipment, timely payment, and access to rapid diagnosis and high-quality supportive care if they fall ill.

Abdulsalami Nasidi, a public health consultant who helped establish the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, told Al Jazeera that the outbreak was “getting out of hand”.

He blamed weak infection control measures and a lack of trust between authorities and affected communities for the continued transmission.

“This is no longer just a national or regional issue; it is a global issue. If it spreads to neighbouring places with lower immunity, it will be a disaster,” Nasidi added.

The WHO currently rates the risk to the global public as low, but warns that the danger inside the DRC remains very high.

Despite the surging cases, Uganda and several health zones in DRC’s Ituri and South Kivu have interrupted transmission, which the WHO said is evidence that rapid detection, decisive leadership, and community cooperation can break the chain of transmission.

At the Vatican on Sunday, Pope Leo offered prayers for the DRC, “in light of the spread of the Ebola epidemic, which is sadly ⁠claiming many lives”.

The pontiff also called for global action to help save lives.

“I urge the international community to ⁠respond in a way that also involves local communities ⁠in prevention efforts to save ⁠as many lives as possible,” he said.

articles.title: College grad reportedly dies in Six Flags roller coaster incident as family sues theme park
articles.excerpt:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A California family reportedly filed a lawsuit accusing Six Flags Magic Mountain of a defective ride design after thei...
articles.body_text:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A California family reportedly filed a lawsuit accusing Six Flags Magic Mountain of a defective ride design after their 22-year-old son suffered fatal head trauma while riding the the X2 attraction.

The incident happened in summer 2022, when Christopher Hawley, a San Diego State University graduate, visited the Los Angeles County theme park with his family, according to Fox 11 Los Angeles. Hawley reportedly collapsed shortly after riding the X2 roller coaster and died the following day.

Separately, the X2 roller coaster was involved in another incident on July 5, 2026, when a rider was found unconscious, prompting the attraction to close for more than a month, KTLA reported.

Christopher’s death was ruled an accident caused by blunt-force head trauma sustained from the attraction, which his family described as exceptionally rough, Fox 11 said.

PANIC AT POPULAR THEME PARK AS STRANDED RIDERS SCRAMBLE TO ESCAPE BROKEN ROLLER COASTER

An aerial view of roller coasters at Six Flags Magic Mountain. Christopher Hawley, 22, reportedly suffered fatal injuries following a ride on the X2 roller coaster.  (Christopher Hawley/Facebook)

His younger brother, Alex, described the ride as intensely violent, saying it jerked passengers around before ending with a jolt that sent their heads slamming into the headrests.

"It was very rough. It just jerked us. It just jerked us all around," Alex told the local station.

"It just jolted us all the way forward and then our heads just swung all the way back into the headrest."

After Christopher stepped off the attraction, he reportedly appeared noticeably unwell, with his face turning very red before suddenly collapsing.

Emergency responders rushed him to a nearby hospital, but he succumbed to his injuries the next day, Fox 11 reported.

STARTLING FOOTAGE FROM AMUSEMENT PARK SHOWS THRILL RIDE HALTED AS GUESTS WAIT IN MIDAIR

The X2 ride, which allegedly caused Christopher Hawley to sustain fatal head trauma, features seats that rotate 360 degrees.   (Christopher Hawley/Facebook)

The family said a surgeon compared Hawley's injuries to shaken baby syndrome, a condition in which violent and sudden forces cause the brain to move rapidly within the skull, potentially resulting in swelling, bruising and bleeding.

"The surgeon had said, he likened it to shaken baby syndrome, that the ride hit his head so hard that it had basically ruptured his brain," Christopher's father, William, told the local station.

Six Flags declined to comment directly on the litigation to Fox News Digital.

However, the amusement park told Fox 11 that the ride remains closed following the separate July 2026 incident involving the unconscious rider.

"The ride remains closed at this time. It has been closed since the evening of July 12th," Six Flags said.

Christopher Hawley was a recent San Diego State University graduate when he died following a roller coaster ride. (Christopher Hawley/Facebook)

A jury trial involving Six Flags, the manufacturer of the X2 roller coaster and park employees is scheduled to begin Sept. 8, according to reports.

The lawsuit also alleges that the defendants failed to adequately warn the public about the ride's risks, the local station said.

X2 has been advertised as one of the theme park's most intense attractions and features seats that rotate 360 degrees.

The Los Angeles County Fire Department and the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Fox News Digital.

Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

articles.title: US territories hit out at Trump plan to explore deep sea mining in the Pacific
articles.excerpt:
US agency releases plan to lease millions of hectares of seabed off the coast of the Northern Mariana Islands and Guam

A US government plan to lease out millions of hectares of seabed near the Marian...
articles.body_text:
US agency releases plan to lease millions of hectares of seabed off the coast of the Northern Mariana Islands and Guam

A US government plan to lease out millions of hectares of seabed near the Mariana Trench for deep sea exploration has drawn opposition from US territories in the Pacific, as the Trump administration remains locked in a race with China for control of critical ocean minerals.

On Tuesday, the Marine Mineral Administration (MMA), an agency under the US department of the interior, released a proposal to auction deep sea mining leases for 28m hectares (69m acres) of seafloor off the coast of the Northern Mariana Islands and Guam.

The leases ​would allow companies to ‌explore the seabed and potentially extract ‌deposits of critical minerals – known as polymetallic nodules – that could be used in batteries, electronics and defence technologies. Many environmental ​groups have ​opposed deep sea mining, arguing that more research is needed on its effects on marine ecosystems.

The Northern Mariana Islands is a self-governing commonwealth of the United States, while Guam is an unincorporated territory of the US.

The governor of the Northern Marianas, David Apatang, has said his government would approach the Trump administration’s proposal “with extreme caution”.

Apatang, while acknowledging the strategic importance of critical minerals, said it was necessary that “no activity, survey or otherwise, takes place without rigorous scientific baseline studies, complete transparency, and explicit protections for our marine resources”.

He said his administration would “thoroughly examine the proposed terms over the next 60 days to ensure that the ecological integrity of our waters and the long-term wellbeing of the [Northern Marianas] are fully safeguarded”.

The Guardian approached the Marine Mineral Administration for comment.

In an earlier statement, the MMA said it had completed an environmental review of proposed commercial leases for critical minerals in the Marianas area. The MMA said it would consider comments from the governor.

A statement from the office of the governor of Guam acknowledged the Trump administration’s focus on national security and strategic needs, but added: “National security cannot mean asking the people of the Pacific to accept environmental risks before those risks are fully understood.

“We’re unequivocally opposed to the deep sea mining efforts in this region,” said Guam’s lieutenant governor, Joshua Tenorio.

He told the Guardian: “The department of interior is giving assurances that mining activity is not going to commence with the awarding of these licences, [but] I think that this is a matter where we can’t really trust that because this has been rapidly evolving.”

The proposed lease notice for deep sea exploration in the Marianas region came just weeks after the initiation of a leasing process for 12.4m hectares (31m acres) of American Samoa’s seafloor, with plans to award contracts in November.

The governor of American Samoa, Nikolau Pula, said his government remained opposed to deep sea mining, noting that untested extraction processes could harm the territory’s tuna industry, which fuels its economy.

On 19 August, environmental groups in American Samoa and Hawaii launched legal proceedings against the US government to halt the proposed auction of seafloor permits around the islands, alleging that federal agencies failed to evaluate the destructive impact mineral extractions could have on marine ecosystems.

In a Hawaii court, Fa’asao Ameika Samoa and the Conservation Council for Hawaii warned that the extraction machinery “can destroy nearly all life in its path” and “stirs up sediments that can introduce toxic substances into the food web and smother seafloor ecosystems”.

“Even just exploring for seabed minerals introduces extremely loud noise into the marine environment that can harm marine mammals and other wildlife,” the complaint reads.

The Marine Mineral Administration was approached about the concerns over the American Samoa leasing process.

Former NBA center Enes Kanter Freedom, who is trying to make his way into women’s basketball, was escorted out of Wintrust Arena during the third quarter Sunday after a heated shouting match with Chicago Sky guard Natasha Cloud.

With the Indiana Fever holding an 81-75 lead during a third-quarter timeout, Cloud began barking toward Freedom, who was seated courtside.

Former basketball player Enes Kanter Freedom and Natasha Cloud #9 of the Chicago Sky yell at one another during the second half against the Indiana Fever at Wintrust Arena in Chicago, Ill., on Aug. 23, 2026. (Getty Images)

Former basketball player Enes Kanter Freedom and Natasha Cloud #9 of the Chicago Sky yell at one another during the second half between the Chicago Sky and the Indiana Fever at Wintrust Arena in Chicago, Ill., on Aug. 23, 2026. (Getty Images)

Freedom responded and stepped toward the floor, prompting security to intervene and usher the 11-year NBA veteran out as the Chicago crowd rained down boos.

WNBA COMMISSIONER CATHY ENGELBERT BLAMES THE WRONG PEOPLE FOR ‘SOWING DIVISIVENESS’ IN TRANSGENDER DEBATE

Immediately after security removed him, Freedom fired back on X: "I just got kicked out of a @WNBA game for supporting WOMEN! Let that sink in, AMERICA!"

He followed with another jab: "It’s always women hating on other women."

WNBA COMMISSIONER CATHY ENGELBERT SENDS TRANS INCLUSION MEMO AFTER ENES FREEDOM, ROYCE WHITE ANNOUNCEMENTS

Former basketball player Enes Kanter Freedom poses courtside prior to the game between the Chicago Sky and the Indiana Fever at Wintrust Arena on Aug. 23, 2026, in Chicago, Ill. (Getty Images)

Cloud previously called America "trash," so Freedom offered to buy her a ticket to China, Russia or Turkey, where she could trade her woke complaints for a firsthand look at actual tyranny. He also arrived Sunday wearing a shirt with the definition of "woman" printed across it, a message Cloud apparently did not appreciate.

After the game, Sky players Azura Stevens and Aicha Coulibaly were asked about Freedom’s ejection.

Stevens quickly shut down the topic, telling reporters, "There was just a fan incident and the security handled it. We’re going to just focus on the game."

She did not take follow-up questions about Kanter Freedom.

Before getting tossed, Freedom spent the afternoon poking the bear.

FORMER NBA STAR ENES KANTER FREEDOM WRITES LETTER TO WNBA OFFICIALLY DECLARING FOR 2027 DRAFT

At halftime, he posted a photo outside an arena restroom with the caption: "It’s halftime and I need to use the restroom… Rules are rules @WNBA."

Enes was also part of a hostile pregame scene outside the arena. A mob of progressive fans confronted Freedom, forcing security to form a shield around the 6-foot-10 former NBA center. One spectator flipped him the bird, while another shouted, "You were sorry in the league!"

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SUPPORTERS RALLY IN CHICAGO, WHILE PROTESTERS SHOWCASE WHAT'S WRONG WITH AMERICA

He posted a video of the confrontation, writing: "We are getting attacked before the @WNBA game in Chicago."

Freedom has taken relentless fire for defending female athletes, including alongside Sophie Cunningham supporters before tipoff.

Caitlin Clark #22 of the Indiana Fever reacts prior to a game against the Chicago Sky at Wintrust Arena on Aug. 23, 2026, in Chicago, Ill. (Getty Images)

Caitlin Clark of the Indiana Fever and DiJonai Carrington of the Chicago Sky collide during the first half at Wintrust Arena in Chicago, Ill., on Aug. 23, 2026. (Getty Images)

Security escorted him out of the building Sunday. Whether the WNBA lets him into another arena now remains to be seen. Either way, Freedom remains unbothered by the noise and willing to take on the league’s policies.

Caitlin Clark's Fever beat Chicago, 113-90.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Requests for comment sent to the Chicago Sky and Wintrust Arena management were not immediately returned.

Enes Kanter Freedom gets thrown out during a regular-season WNBA game between the Indiana Fever and the Chicago Sky on Aug. 23, 2026, at Wintrust Arena in Chicago, Ill. (Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

articles.title: California dad paralyzed from neck down after diving into ocean to rescue child
articles.excerpt: Nathaniel Rai, 10, shares new details in an interview with Fox News Digital about his terrifying drowning experience and the remarkable friendship his family formed with the teen lifeguard who rescued...
articles.body_text:
Nathaniel Rai, 10, shares new details in an interview with Fox News Digital about his terrifying drowning experience and the remarkable friendship his family formed with the teen lifeguard who rescued him.

A California father of five was paralyzed from the neck down after entering the ocean in an effort to help a young child who his family said was caught in a rip current.

Josh Collette, 42, was spending time with his family at Riviera Beach in San Clemente, California, on Aug. 15, when a child believed to be 7- or 8-years-old became caught in a rip current, the man's sister, Hillary Collette, told KTLA.

The child’s mother first entered the water to go after her child, but Josh Collette ran past her and dove into the ocean in an effort to help the child, Hillary Collette told the outlet.

GEORGIA TEACHER, FATHER HAILED AS HERO AFTER DYING TO SAVE GIRL FROM MYRTLE BEACH RIP CURRENT

Josh Collette was paralyzed from the neck down after heroically diving into the ocean to help a young child who was caught in a rip current. (GoFundMe)

As he entered the water, Collette’s sister said he struck either a sandbar or rocks and was immediately injured.

Several people then rushed to his aid and helped pull him from the water. He told his wife right away that he believed he had broken his neck.

The child Josh Collette was attempting to help was safely pulled out of the water before Collette was brought from the water, his sister said.

Collette’s sister said doctors told the family that Josh Collette was paralyzed from the neck down.

Josh Collette inadvertently hit either a sandbar or rocks after entering the water, injuring him immediately. (GoFundMe)

His sister said he was unable to speak but communicated by moving his lips; she said the family expects him to regain his ability to speak.

His family created a GoFundMe as they prepare to help with medical bills, long-term therapy and support for the family as they navigate the long and difficult recovery ahead.

"Josh was hurt in an ocean accident on Sat Aug 15th he has a spinal cord injury," a family member wrote on the fundraiser. "The road ahead will be long, and the recovery will not be easy, we’re holding on to hope."

"We believe in miracles! We’ve already seen so many and thank everyone for the love, support, and prayers!" the fundraiser added. "Please keep praying for miracles! Its working!"

'HERO' FATHER DROWNS SAVING HIS 12-YEAR-OLD SON FROM RIP CURRENT AT POPULAR BEACH DESTINATION, FAMILY SAYS

Josh Collette with his wife and five children. (GoFundMe)

In an update shared on Friday, the family said it will take some time for him to no longer need medicine. The family also shared a picture of Josh Collette from his hospital bed.

"Yesterday was so positive and productive! So, it was hard to have a day with less progress. This guy hates medicine! He's trying hard to get off of everything... but, that's going to take some time. Thank you so much for all the prayers, love, and support. We love you all so much and feel so loved by all the help you’ve given us. We’re hanging in there and so grateful for all of you," the family wrote on the fundraiser.

The GoFundMe has raised nearly $110,000 as of Sunday night.

articles.title: Louisiana girl, 8, dies after contracting suspected brain-eating amoeba linked to lake swim
articles.excerpt: Fox News senior medical analyst Dr. Marc Siegel warns beachgoers about the rise of Vibrio vulnificus, a deadly flesh-eating bacteria found in warm salt waters. Already nine cases reported in Florida a...
articles.body_text:
Fox News senior medical analyst Dr. Marc Siegel warns beachgoers about the rise of Vibrio vulnificus, a deadly flesh-eating bacteria found in warm salt waters. Already nine cases reported in Florida and five deaths in Louisiana.

Lillian Smart, an 8-year-old girl who health officials believe contracted a brain-eating amoeba while swimming in a northern Louisiana lake, died Saturday at a Ruston hospital from an infection linked to the pathogen.

Lillian died one day after celebrating her eighth birthday.

"The injuries to her brain were too severe for her little body to recover from," the Smart family said in a statement posted Sunday morning on Facebook. "Everyone did everything they could to keep her here. We are heartbroken and honestly do not know what to do next. How do we put one foot in front of the other without our girl?"

The Louisiana Department of Health announced Wednesday that a state resident had been hospitalized after becoming infected with Naegleria fowleri, a microscopic amoeba that can cause a rare and often deadly brain infection.

MICHIGAN REPORTS 2 DEATHS IN RARE PARASITE OUTBREAK THAT HAS SICKENED MORE THAN 11,000

Lillian Smart, center, is pictured with her parents. The 8-year-old died Saturday after her family said she contracted Naegleria fowleri. (Facebook/Love for Lillian Smart)

State health officials have not publicly identified Lillian as the patient referenced in the announcement. Her family, however, said on social media that she had been admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit at a Ruston hospital and identified Naegleria fowleri as the cause of her illness.

The health department said the infection in the case it announced was most likely acquired while the patient was swimming in Lake Claiborne shortly before becoming ill.

A representative for the Louisiana Department of Health did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Louisiana Department of Health records identify three previous deaths associated with Naegleria fowleri in the state since 2011.

BEACHGOERS WARNED AFTER DEADLY 'FLESH-EATING' BACTERIA KILLS 5 IN SOUTHERN STATE

Lillian Smart, 8, died Saturday after her family said she contracted Naegleria fowleri, a rare amoeba that can cause a deadly brain infection. (Facebook/Love for Lillian Smart)

Two happened in 2011. A 20-year-old man in St. Bernard Parish died after using tap water to rinse his sinuses, while a 51-year-old woman in DeSoto Parish died after using tap water for a similar purpose.

In 2013, a 4-year-old boy contracted the amoeba while visiting a home in St. Bernard Parish, where he had played on a slip-and-slide. State officials later reported that CDC testing detected Naegleria fowleri in the parish water system.

Naegleria fowleri causes primary amoebic meningoencephalitis, or PAM, an extremely rare brain infection that can develop when contaminated water enters the nose and the amoeba travels to the brain. People cannot become infected by swallowing contaminated water.

The amoeba is not found in saltwater or properly chlorinated swimming pools.

DEADLY BACTERIA FOUND IN WATERS NEAR LUXURY VACATION DESTINATION AHEAD OF SUMMER

A birthday memory jar invited loved ones to share favorite memories and messages for Lillian Smart ahead of her eighth birthday. (Facebook/Love for Lillian Smart)

Symptoms typically begin with headache, fever, nausea and vomiting before progressing to a stiff neck, seizures and coma. Symptoms generally appear about five days after infection, and the disease can lead to death within about one to two weeks.

About 97% of people who develop PAM die from the infection, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

The CDC reported two PAM cases nationwide last year. Of the 173 infections documented over roughly the past 90 years, nearly 91% occurred in July and August.

Brittany Miller is a Fox News Digital breaking news writer and former Independent reporter who graduated from Syracuse University in 2023.

articles.title: Australian shark attack victim grateful for 'second chance at life'
articles.excerpt:
Leah Stewart was bitten by a shark at Sydney's Coogee Beach during a morning swim

An Australian woman bitten by a shark at a popular Sydney beach earlier this year says she has been given a "second c...
articles.body_text:
Leah Stewart was bitten by a shark at Sydney's Coogee Beach during a morning swim

An Australian woman bitten by a shark at a popular Sydney beach earlier this year says she has been given a "second chance at life" and will be making the most of it.

Leah Stewart, 35, was mauled by a shark during a morning swim at Coogee Beach in June, suffering multiple bites to her arms and legs, amid a spate of attacks in Australia.

The mother-of-one was placed in an induced coma and had several surgeries, including having one of her arms amputated.

In an online post on Monday, she thanked her supporters who have raised more than AU$550,000 (US$394,000; £289,000) for her, saying her recovery has been "incredibly difficult" but she is making "remarkable" progress.

"After what has been an incredibly difficult few months, I'm so happy that I've progressed enough to build some independence, and I can finally see some light after all of this," Stewart wrote, in her first comments since the attack.

"I want you to know that I feel like I've been given a second chance at life, and I'm not going to waste it."

Stewart said she had been "overwhelmed" by the support from family, friends and "even strangers", adding that the "you've inspired me to get better, not bitter".

An online fundraiser for her would now be closed, she wrote, with the money raised giving her the chance to recover at home as well as "options for further medical treatment down the road".

"I still have a long way to go, but my recovery has been remarkable, and a huge part of that is because of the absolute army of love, support, prayers and encouragement surrounding my family and I from all over the world."

There have been a spate of shark attacks in Australia this year, with four attacks over a two-day period in January, including one on a 12-year-old boy who later died from his injuries.

In May, a man was killed by a shark in Queensland while spearfishing and in Western Australia, a father-of-two died after he was attacked by a 4m (13ft) shark.

articles.title: Trump shrugs off assassination attempts, remarking 'only consequential presidents get shot'
articles.excerpt:
President Donald Trump remarked on the multiple assassination attempts against him during an interview with his former personal lawyer Michael Cohen.

President Donald Trump laughed off the multiple a...
articles.body_text:
President Donald Trump remarked on the multiple assassination attempts against him during an interview with his former personal lawyer Michael Cohen.

President Donald Trump laughed off the multiple assassination attempts against him, remarking that "only consequential presidents get shot" during an interview with his former personal lawyer Michael Cohen on Sunday.

Cohen released the second part of his two-part interview with Trump in which the two dived into additional topics, such as reports that Trump secretly boarded a separate military jet in response to a credible Iranian threat against his life. The former Trump critic pointed out that this was only the latest in a series of attempts on the president's life.

"I'm so nauseated by them," Cohen said. "There is a huge difference between vehemently disagreeing with a policy and then trying to literally assassinate the President of the United States."

TRUMP'S DECADE OF ASSASSINATION THREATS RUNS FROM BUTLER SHOOTING TO LATEST GOLF CLUB BREACH

President Donald Trump reacted to assassination attempts against him after reports that he had switched plans to avoid an Iranian threat. (Evan Vucci/Reuters)

"The one thing I would say to that. If you read, only consequential presidents get shot," Trump quipped.

"Then do me a favor, please don't be consequential. How's that?" Cohen said.

"I know. Maybe I'll have to become less consequential," Trump responded.

Trump acknowledged that he has a "dangerous" job but added that he has "great people" looking after him.

I SERVED AS TRUMP’S NSA. SCOTUS NEED TO STOP COURTS PUTTING THE PRESIDENT'S SECURITY AT RISK

"Obviously, it's gotten much, much tougher over the years. But it is true, consequential. You look at the people that were shot. You look at the people, even the attempts, but non-consequential presidents lead a much nicer life. You can see that with some of our recent presidents where nothing was ever even thought about," Trump said.

President Donald Trump told Michael Cohen that "non-consequential" presidents tend to lead nicer lives. (AP Photo/Evan Vucci)

Cohen was originally a key witness in two New York cases against Trump and a frequent critic of the president prior to his interview on Thursday. In a Substack post he penned detailing the stunning reunion that was their first public conversation in nearly a decade, Cohen emphasized the importance of forgiveness despite the backlash he faced for the interview.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

"Colossians 3:13 says: ‘Bear with each other and forgive one another if any of you has a grievance against someone. Forgive as the Lord forgave you,’" he wrote. "That verse isn’t merely some theological footnote to what is happening between Donald Trump and me. It is the foundation of it."

President Donald Trump and Michael Cohen spoke publicly for the first time in nearly a decade during a radio interview. (Jim Watson / AFP via Getty Images; Jim Watson / AFP via Getty Images)

Fox News' Brian Flood contributed to this report.

Lindsay Kornick is an associate editor for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to lindsay.kornick@fox.com and on Twitter: @lmkornick.

articles.title: Minnesota tree trimmer charged in coworker’s death after on-the-job horseplay turns deadly
articles.excerpt:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A tree-trimming employee has been charged with manslaughter after allegedly crushing his coworker’s head with a hydrau...
articles.body_text:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A tree-trimming employee has been charged with manslaughter after allegedly crushing his coworker’s head with a hydraulic grapple while the pair were reportedly "f—ing around" on the job, according to Minnesota authorities.

The incident happened in Apple Valley on Thursday when Christopher Boone Crimmins, 34, was operating machinery on the back of a truck while his coworker, Tyler Anthony Lynch, 26, was on the ground cleaning up branches, according to a criminal complaint filed by Dakota County.

Responding to reports of an incident, police discovered Lynch lying on the ground with "a significant amount of blood around him and significant trauma to his head," the complaint said.

Lynch was pronounced dead at the scene, according to the county.

WORKERS WARNED OHIO TRENCH WAS TOO DEEP BUT WERE TOLD TO ENTER MINUTES BEFORE FATAL CAVE-IN: REPORT

Christopher Crimmins has been accused of recklessly operating a boom when he allegedly killed his coworker. (Dakota County Jail )

Authorities said Crimmins was operating a boom, a movable mechanical arm attached to a truck, when he and Lynch began messing around with their shadows.

"He and the Victim were ‘f—ing around’ and saw that the sunlight was casting shadows of both the grapple and of the Victim on the street," the criminal complaint said.

While looking at the shadows, Crimmins allegedly maneuvered the grapple so that its shadow appeared to grab Lynch’s shadow.

However, he did not realize that the grapple itself was moving toward Lynch’s head.

TWO WORKERS KILLED, SEVERAL INJURED AFTER EXPLOSIONS TEAR THROUGH OHIO RECYCLING FACILITY

An employee operates a grapple to remove a tree from a residential property. A Minnesota tree-trimming worker was charged with second-degree manslaughter after allegedly crushing a coworker’s head with a hydraulic grapple while the two were horsing around with their shadows on the job. (Robert Nickelsberg/Getty Images)

"Crimmins was not monitoring the actual grapple or Lynch. He then opened and closed the grapple, crushing Lynch’s head," the Dakota County Attorney's Office said.

A witness also saw the incident unfold and said the grapple appeared to "hit or pinch" Lynch’s head as it approached him.

WORKERS KILLED AND MANY TREATED AFTER REFINERY CHEMICAL RELEASE AS INVESTIGATORS PROBE CAUSE

Officers observed blood on the grapple, which was directly above Lynch, according to the complaint.

Authorities alleged Crimmins was responsible for the incident through negligence, saying he created an "unreasonable risk" and "consciously takes chances of causing death or great bodily harm to another."

A hydraulic grapple grips a large tree branch during a tree-trimming job. (Matthias Rietschel/picture alliance via Getty Images)

Crimmins has been charged with one felony count of second-degree manslaughter. If convicted, he faces a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison and a $20,000 fine.

Officials said Crimmins was being held at the Dakota County Jail. Bail was set at $40,000 without conditions or $20,000 with conditions.

Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

articles.title: WNBA has 'no idea what they're about to face,' Enes Kanter Freedom says as league takes on trans athlete issue
articles.excerpt:
Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom talks about how he's holding the WNBA accountable regarding its transgender policy on 'My View with Lara Trump.'

Enes Kanter Freedom said Saturday he was "prepar...
articles.body_text:
Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom talks about how he's holding the WNBA accountable regarding its transgender policy on 'My View with Lara Trump.'

Enes Kanter Freedom said Saturday he was "prepared" to play in the WNBA

Freedom drummed up some controversy earlier this month when he "declared" for the WNBA Draft after lack of support for Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham and her belief that transgender women shouldn’t have to compete against females.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Enes Kanter Freedom attends the Algemeiner 50th Anniversary J100 Gala at The Ziegfeld Ballroom in New York City on Nov. 29, 2022. (Patrick McMullan via Getty Images)

With the WNBA lacking clarity on its gender eligibility policy and players and coaches seemingly supporting trans athletes’ abilities to join the WNBA, Freedom decided to attempt to make the league put up or shut up.

Freedom appeared on Fox News Channel’s "My View with Lara Trump" on Saturday to talk about the issue.

"I think I will be the best draft pick in WNBA history, literally," he said.

Freedom said Golden State Valkyries star Gabby Williams’ support for trans athletes and Minnesota Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve’s "support trans kids" shirt was what led him to this moment.

"So, there’s other major sports that obviously closed that loophole," he said. "They added ‘biological female’ or ‘born female’ in their collective bargaining. But when I look at them, the WNBA, they didn’t have kind of, you know, reference to biological or anything like that. And all the coaches, I was watching this, and I believe the coach of Minnesota came out with a ‘trans kids belong’ (shirt), so I was like, if no one’s against it and all the coaches are OK with it, think about how much money I can bring, think about all the endorsement deals.

Enes Kanter of the New York Knicks is in action against the Miami Heat during the first half at American Airlines Arena in Miami, Fla., on Oct. 24, 2018. (Getty Images)

League officials met to discuss the trans athlete topic and later put out a statement, saying they were continuing the conversation but needled the media for allegedly sewing division in the sport and called out "bad-faith" efforts to undermine the organization.

"The WNBA has no idea what they’re about to face. They’re still trying to figure out what a woman is," he said. "So, let’s see if they can figure that out. So, let’s see what kind of rules that they’re gonna come up with."

OutKick reached out to the WNBA for comment.

Cunningham took her stance on trans athletes in women and girls’ sports in an interview with ESPN.

"I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I’m like, ‘I never once said that.’ I think that I am here to extend love. But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men."

Kanter told Trump that he believed Cunningham was an "American hero."

"First of all, I want to say is, she is an American hero," he said. "Everywhere she goes I see now a lot of people are coming out an actually defending her. But obviously, if you are standing up for something you believe in, you’re gonna get hate all the time.

"But I think she’s inspiring not only the players in the WNBA but girls from all over the world. Not only in America because I get so many messages and they’re saying that, from all over the world, they say, ‘Hey, if you ever see Sophie Cunningham, can you please say hi to her?’"

Several rallies have taken place before WNBA games in support of Cunningham. The latest occurred before the Fever’s game against the New York Liberty on Saturday.

Ryan Gaydos is a senior editor for Fox News Digital.
